instructions:
# PipesHub MCP — instructions for the LLM

PipesHub is the user's workplace AI platform. It indexes their documents,
knowledge base content, and connector sources (Drive, Box, Confluence,
Slack, Jira, Gmail, ...). When in doubt, the answer is in PipesHub.

## Default: search, then read

For any question the user's PipesHub-indexed data could answer — company
policies, processes, decisions, history, who said what, "what do we know
about X", anything naming PipesHub or a connected source (Drive / Box /
Confluence / Slack / Gmail / Jira / ...) — do NOT answer from your own
knowledge. Retrieve and read it yourself:

1. `pipeshub_search` for the topic, names, or phrases. Try other wording,
   or narrow with `apps` / `kb`, when the first results miss.
2. `pipeshub_get_record_content` on the records that matter (the hit's
   `recordId`), and answer from what they say. Search passages are a
   sample of a record, not all of it.

A named record (issue key, link, external ID) starts with `mode:"lookup"`
instead, and "how many / all / every" with `mode:"navigate"` (below).

Read the record whole whenever missing part of it could make the answer
wrong:

- Summarize / TL;DR / key points / takeaways / action items of a doc.
- Extract or list ALL of something (dates, owners, requirements, ...).
- Check whether / where a doc mentions something.
- Translate, rewrite, outline, review, or reformat a doc.
- Compare named docs (fetch each `recordId`).

That returns one record, which is not always the whole conversation: Slack
thread replies are separate records ("Reply Count: N" means they are not in
the text; `mode:"thread"` reads the whole thread). A long record, such as
a GitHub PR with its diffs, would exceed your tool-output limit, so it comes
back in parts: pass `query` to get the passages that matter first, or
follow the closing `Next:` line to read on.

## `pipeshub_chat` is optional

`pipeshub_chat` runs PipesHub's own assistant over a few passages it
retrieves itself. An agent that searches and reads for itself is as
accurate, with fewer wrong claims, at lower cost and latency, so a client
may leave chat out. Use it only when you cannot run your own search-and-read
loop, when the user asks for PipesHub's answer, to run an org agent, or to
take an action the user asked for through their connected tools.
Do NOT call it to cross-check, fill gaps in, or summarize what you searched
and read: it reads less than you did. Search again with other wording.

Its answer is a synthesis of a few passages, never a whole document, so
treat it as a lead: confirm a specific ID, status, date, owner, or "merged /
shipped" in the cited record before stating it. "Not found" means not in
what it read, not that it does not exist.

It can also take actions through the user's connected tools (for example
create a ticket or send an email). Actions are on unless an admin has
turned them off. Ask it questions, and never ask it to write unless the
user asked for that action.

## Other tools

- `pipeshub_download_record` — when the user wants the file as stored
  (download, attach, open). Never to read or summarize — that is
  `pipeshub_get_record_content` `mode:"content"`, which returns
  parsed text with a metadata header. `convertTo` is only
  `application/pdf`.
- `pipeshub_directory` — people, groups, teams, and `whoami` lookups.
  Not for documents or files — that is `pipeshub_search`.
- `pipeshub_sources` — call once at the start of a session to discover
  which connectors / KB / models are available, then cache the result.
- `pipeshub_agents` — list the org's configured **agents** (specialized
  assistants with their own prompt, tools, and knowledge scope).

## Knowledge Sources

A source (an app connector or a KB) holds record groups (a project, space,
drive, folder), which hold records (one ticket, page, file). Records nest —
an epic over its stories, a page over its child pages.

**Every tool returns metadata or content.**

- `pipeshub_search` / `pipeshub_chat` — content, but only a ranked sample of
  passages: never every record that matches, never a complete list of what
  exists. Search returns one entry per record with up to 3 passages; read a
  record whole with `mode:"content"`.
- `mode:"lookup"` and `mode:"navigate"` — metadata: recordIds, fields, and
  structure. No document text. `mode:"content"` — one record's text, in
  parts; `mode:"thread"` — a whole Slack thread.

**Combining them.** Search finds a starting point by wording; navigate on a
`recordId` reveals what search structurally cannot — siblings, children,
in-source links (`Related`), and the group's total count. `Related` omits
Slack messages and pages that only mention a record. To find Slack discussion
of a PR or ticket, search for its number or URL with the Slack connector id in
`apps`; to find a page that mentions it, run the same search without `apps`,
across every source. For a question that must be
exhaustive ("all", "how many", "every"), do NOT count search hits or trust a
chat answer:
navigate the record group, which reports the real total. For a
record's siblings, navigate its parent — take the id from the `Path` line.

**A named record** — an issue key, a Confluence / Drive / Slack link, an
external ID → `mode:"lookup"` FIRST. It returns that record's metadata (for a
ticket: status, assignee, priority, dates) plus its `recordId`, which often
answers the question outright. Never guess a `recordId`.

For search, pass a connector id from `pipeshub_sources` as `apps: ["<id>"]`
and a collection id (`kind: "knowledgeBase"`) as `kb: ["<id>"]`. Any source
id works as `nodeId` to navigate. Navigate and lookup end in a `Next:` line
naming the exact follow-up call — follow it.

## Agents

Some orgs configure **agents** for specific jobs (e.g. a Slack messenger, a
Jira ticket creator, a Salesforce CRM updater). To run a turn against an
agent, call `pipeshub_chat` with its `agentId` (from `pipeshub_agents`).

- The user names a system/action that maps to an agent (e.g. "post to
  Slack", "create a Jira ticket", "update the Salesforce deal") → call
  `pipeshub_agents`, pick the matching agent, and use it.
- A plain question about the org's knowledge → search and read, above.

**If you are unsure which agent fits the request**, call
`pipeshub_agents` FIRST and read the returned names/descriptions, then
either pick the best match or present the list to the user and let them
choose. Do NOT guess an agent blindly, and do NOT refuse — list the agents
and decide from real data. The list may be empty (no agents configured).
When no agent fits an action the user asked for, call `pipeshub_chat`
without an `agentId`: plain chat can use the user's connected tools.

## Conversation lifecycle

`pipeshub_chat` starts and continues conversations (plain or with an
`agentId`). On the first turn omit `conversationId`; on every later
turn pass back the `conversationId` it returned (with the same
`agentId` if you used one). Server-side context is preserved — do NOT
replay prior messages. Start a fresh conversation only when the user
explicitly asks to clear context.

arguments.description: Optional. The user's request to route. Provide it to have the guidance applied to a concrete request; omit it to just load the routing guidance as a seed system prompt at the start of a session.
arguments.name: query

prompts.description: Load PipesHub tool-routing guidance so the assistant picks the correct tool (search and read by default; chat / agents / directory) and lists agents with pipeshub_agents when unsure which route fits the query.
prompts.name: pipeshub-assistant

tools.description:
List the PipesHub **agents** configured for this org, each with its
capabilities.

Agents are specialized assistants (custom system prompt, tools, knowledge
scope). To converse with one, take its `agentId` and pass it to
`pipeshub_chat`'s `agentId` argument.

Each agent is returned as:
`{ agentId, name, description, systemPrompt, startMessage, tags, webSearch,
isActive, toolsets, knowledge }`.
- `toolsets` — what the agent can DO: each `{ name, tools }` where `name`
  is the connector (e.g. `jira`, `gmail`) and `tools` are the runnable
  tool ids (e.g. `jira.create_issue`, `gmail.send_email`).
- `knowledge` — what the agent can READ: each `{ name, type }` (e.g.
  `Confluence-2` / `Confluence`).

**Route on `toolsets`/`knowledge`, not the name** — names and descriptions
are often generic or misleading. Match the request to the agent whose tools can
actually perform it (e.g. "create a Jira ticket" → the agent whose toolset is
`jira` and whose tools include `jira.create_issue`). If NO agent has a tool
for the requested action, don't force an unrelated agent: call `pipeshub_chat`
without an `agentId`, which can use the user's connected tools.

The list **may be empty** (no agents configured). For plain Q&A when no
specific agent is needed, use `pipeshub_search` and read the records. Use `agentId` everywhere an agent is referenced.

search.description: Optional case-insensitive substring match across agent name, description, and tags. Omit to return every agent.

tools.name: pipeshub_agents

tools.description:
Optional. Ask PipesHub's own assistant. Its answer is a synthesis of a
few retrieved passages — never a whole document, never a complete list.

**If you can call tools, answer the question yourself:** `pipeshub_search`,
then read the records that matter with `pipeshub_get_record_content`
(`mode:"navigate"` for what is under an epic, space or folder, and for
every "how many" / "all"). That is as accurate as adding this tool, with fewer wrong claims,
at lower cost and latency.

Use this tool only when you cannot run your own search-and-read loop, when
the user asks for PipesHub's answer, to run an org agent (pass an
`agentId` from `pipeshub_agents` to use that agent's own prompt, tools
and knowledge), or to take an action the user asked for through their
connected tools, with no `agentId` when no agent fits. Do NOT call it to
cross-check or fill gaps in what you searched and read; search again
instead.

It answers from the org's indexed sources (Drive, Box, Confluence, Slack,
Gmail, Jira, the org's KB, ...) and from the live web. It undercounts
"how many" / "all" and will not say so.

**It can also act.** Actions are on unless an admin turns them off: the
assistant may use the user's connected tools (e.g. create a Jira ticket,
send an email) with their credentials. Never ask it to write unless the
user asked for that.

**Conversation lifecycle**: omit `conversationId` on the first turn and
capture it from the response. Pass it on follow-ups: the server keeps the
context, so do NOT replay earlier messages, and `filters` is ignored.
Omit it again only when the user asks to start over.

The response holds the AI's `answer`; `citations`, each with its
`number` (the [N] in the answer) and the cited `passage`; `claims`,
each cited sentence with `quotes` copied from its cited text; and
`uncitedSentences`. Treat the answer as a lead: before stating a specific
ID, status, date, owner, or that something merged or shipped, check the
claim's quotes, else confirm it in the cited record (`recordId` →
`mode:"content"`). A quote shows where to look, not that the claim is
right. "Not found" means not in what it read, not that it does not exist.
To download a cited document, call `pipeshub_download_record`.

agentId.description: Optional PipesHub agent to converse with — the `agentId` from `pipeshub_agents`. When set, this turn runs against that agent's configuration (prompt, tools, knowledge). On follow-up turns pass the SAME `agentId` together with the `conversationId` returned by the previous call. Omit for a plain (non-agent) conversation. If unsure which agent to use, call `pipeshub_agents` first to see the options.

conversationId.description: Existing conversation id to continue. Omit on the FIRST turn; on every subsequent turn pass the `conversationId` returned by the previous call. Server-side message history is preserved — do NOT replay prior messages.

filters.description: Which sources the answer may use. Leave out to use all sources. Only works on the FIRST turn; later turns keep the first turn's sources.

apps.description: Connector ids to use. Get them from `pipeshub_sources`, where `kind` is "connector". Collection ids go in `kb`, not here.

kb.description: Collection (knowledge base) ids to use. Get them from `pipeshub_sources`, where `kind` is "knowledgeBase".

modelKey.description: Model id to use (from `pipeshub_sources` `llmModels[*].modelKey`). Defaults to the org's default LLM.

query.description: The user's question or message for this turn.

tools.name: pipeshub_chat

tools.description:
Look up people, groups, and teams in PipesHub. Five actions — pick
`action`. Not for documents or files: that is `pipeshub_search`.

- `whoami` — the caller's id, email, full name. Use before `get_user`
  on yourself. Errors if the credential is expired or revoked.
- `list_users` — page org users; `search` matches name or email.
- `get_user` — full `User` for one `userId`.
- `list_groups` — org groups with `userCount`; `search` matches name.
- `list_my_teams` — teams the caller is on, with `canEdit` /
  `canDelete` / `canManageMembers`; `search` matches name.

Omit `page`/`limit` for the first page (`page` 1). No match is an
empty `users`/`groups`/`teams` array, not an error.
`pagination.hasNextPage` (teams: `hasNext`) says whether to request
the next page.

action.description:
What to do:
- `whoami` — return the authenticated user's identity, confirmed against the server. No other args needed.
- `list_users` — paginated list of org users. Optional `page`, `limit`, `search` (substring match against name or email).
- `get_user` — full profile for one user. Required `userId`. Use `whoami` to find your own id first if needed.
- `list_groups` — paginated list of user groups (with `userCount`). Optional `search` matches group name.
- `list_my_teams` — teams the authenticated user belongs to, with capability flags. Optional `search` matches team name.

limit.description: Items per page for list_* (1–100). Omit for the action default: 50 users, 25 groups, 100 teams.

page.description: 1-based page for list_* actions. Omit for page 1.

search.description: Substring match on list_users (name or email), list_groups (name), and list_my_teams (name). An empty list means no match, not an error.

userId.description: Required when `action` is `get_user`. 24-character ObjectId. Take it from `whoami` (yourself) or from a `list_users` hit.

tools.name: pipeshub_directory

annotations.title: Download a document by record id

tools.description:
Download the file as stored for one record — not PipesHub's parsed
content, metadata header, or summary.

Use this when the user wants the file itself (download, attach, open).
Get `recordId` from a chat citation or a `pipeshub_search` hit.

Do not use this to read, summarize, or answer "what does this doc
say?" regardless of format. That is `pipeshub_get_record_content`
`mode:"content"`. Text formats come back inline; images, audio, and
binary as base64.

`convertTo` accepts only `application/pdf`; anything else is ignored.

convertTo.description: The only conversion target connectors honour is `application/pdf` (the MIME type, not `pdf`). A bare `pdf` is ignored and the original file is returned with no error. Omit for the file as stored. Does not parse the document — use `pipeshub_get_record_content` `mode:"content"` for that.

recordId.description: Record identifier — usually a UUID for connector-sourced records or a 24-character ObjectId for uploaded records. Get it from a chat citation (`citations[*].recordId`) or from a `pipeshub_search` hit.

tools.name: pipeshub_download_record

tools.description:
Four operations on the org's records. Pick by what you hold:

  `mode:"lookup"`   — a URL, issue key (PA-1787), or external ID
                    → its recordId plus the record's metadata
  `mode:"navigate"` — a question about structure: what is under X,
                    what links to Y → browses the hierarchy
  `mode:"content"`  — a recordId, and you need that record's text
  `mode:"thread"`   — a Slack message whose whole thread you need

**`mode:"content"` (default)** — the only way to read one record's full
text. Use it whenever missing part of the document could make the answer
wrong: summarize, extract or list ALL of something, check whether or where
a doc mentions X, review, or compare named docs. `pipeshub_chat` cannot do
these — it never sees a whole document.

Judge by the user's INTENT, not their keywords: "what's this doc about?",
"walk me through the report", "anything in here about Y?" are all
full-content tasks. Get the `recordId` from a `pipeshub_search` top hit, a
chat citation, or `mode:"lookup"`.

Returns a metadata header then the parsed text, up to `maxChars`. A long
record comes in parts, ending in a `Next:` line naming the next call.
GitHub PR records include diffs and can exceed your tool-output limit:
pass `query` to get relevant passages first.
`No record found` may mean it exists but is not indexed yet (newer
servers: a `Not indexed:` line). A missing id is a 403.

It returns one record, not always the whole conversation: a Slack record is
one burst of messages, thread replies are separate records, and "Reply
Count: N" means they are not in this text. `mode:"thread"` on any of
them reads the whole thread.

**`mode:"navigate"`** — browse the hierarchy: RecordGroup (project /
space / drive / folder) → Record (epic / story / page / file) → children,
with breadcrumbs, related links and record IDs.

Use it when the question depends on structure rather than wording: what is
under this epic, which pages sit in this space, what is linked to this
ticket, what is in this folder — and every "how many" / "all of" / "every"
question. Search ranks by content; only this shows how records relate, and
only this gives a count you can trust.

Omit `nodeId` for a flat listing of everything reachable, most recently
updated first — the usual starting point. A URL, an issue key, or a
`pipeshub_sources` id also works and resolves automatically.

Pass `depth:2` or `depth:3` to see several levels in ONE call — an epic's
stories AND their subtasks, a space's pages AND their children — instead of
one call per level. Use it whenever the question needs an overview of a
hierarchy rather than a single node.

Opening a record also prints that record's own metadata — for a ticket,
status, assignee, priority and dates — so a question about one record is
often answered by this call alone. It returns no document text; for that,
re-call with `mode:"content"`.

Returns `Path` breadcrumbs, the current node's metadata, a children listing
carrying `record_id=` or `node_id=` per row plus the group's total
(`Children 1-50 of 61`), `Related` cross-references, and a `Next:` line.
One page is usually every child, so only pass `page:2` when that `Next:`
line says more exist.

`Related` lists only links recorded inside a source (Jira issue links,
GitHub blocked-by), not Slack messages or pages that mention the record. To
find discussion of a PR or ticket, `pipeshub_search` for its number or URL
with the Slack connector id in `apps`.

**`mode:"lookup"`** — turn an external reference into a recordId, the first
step whenever the question names one. Returns that record's metadata (for a
ticket: status, assignee, priority, dates) plus its recordId, which
`mode:"navigate"` takes to list what is under it and `mode:"content"` takes
to read it.

Handles Jira keys and URLs, Confluence, Drive, Slack permalinks, Linear,
Notion, ServiceNow sys_id, SharePoint, Gmail/Outlook, and any connector
whose records index a web URL. Resolution searches ALL connectors you can
access, regardless of any source filter you used elsewhere.

A miss is a 200 with empty `matches` and the input echoed in
`not_found_identifiers` — that may mean no-access, not non-existence. Use
`mode:"navigate"` to confirm the record exists before telling the user it
does not. If `ambiguous` is true, pick from `matches` rather than taking
the first.

Navigate and lookup return a rendered text view whose closing `Next:` line
names the exact follow-up call — follow it. When presenting a record, link
it using the `Web URL` from its metadata header (when present).

connectorName.description: Optional hint that prioritises resolution order, e.g. `JIRA`, `CONFLUENCE`, `GOOGLE_DRIVE`, `SLACK`. It cannot widen the search beyond the connectors you can already access. Useful on a retry when a lookup came back empty.

createdAfter.description: Filter children by source creation time. ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DD`, or a full datetime that MUST carry a timezone offset — a naive datetime is rejected rather than assumed to be UTC.

createdBefore.description: Filter children by source creation time. `YYYY-MM-DD` is inclusive of the whole day.

depth.description: Levels of descendants to return in one call. Above 1, the listing is a flat list of all descendants down to that level rather than only direct children, and each row carries its own `level`.

identifiers.description: The reference(s) to resolve: a URL, an issue key such as `PA-1787`, or a bare external system ID. Paste each exactly as you found it — tracking parameters and fragments are handled. Pass a single string, or an array of up to 10 to resolve them in one call. Required when `mode` is `lookup`.

limit.description: Children per page. The minimum is 50 — smaller values are rejected rather than silently raised.

maxChars.description: Content and thread modes: most characters of text to return. The default (40000, about 10k tokens) fits common tool-output limits; raise it only if your client accepts larger results.

mode.description: `content` (default) reads a record's text by `recordId`, in parts when it is long. `thread` reads the whole Slack thread a message belongs to. `lookup` resolves a URL / issue key / external ID to a recordId. `navigate` browses the knowledge graph tree.

modifiedAfter.description: Filter children by source modification time. Same formats as `createdAfter`.

modifiedBefore.description: Filter children by source modification time. Same formats as `createdBefore`.

nodeId.description: The node to open. Take it from a `record_id=` or `node_id=` shown in a previous navigate or lookup response, from a search hit's `recordId`, or from a `pipeshub_sources` id — a KB or connector id opens that source directly. Omit it entirely for the flat listing of everything reachable, newest first — the usual starting point. A URL or an issue key such as `PA-1787` also works: it is resolved to its record automatically, so no separate lookup is needed.

nodeTypes.description: Restrict children to these node types, e.g. `["record", "folder"]`.

query.description: Content mode: what you are looking for in this record. When the record is longer than `maxChars`, the passages most relevant to it come back first, with the skipped block ranges marked. Ignored when `startBlock` is given.

recordId.description: Record identifier — usually a UUID for connector-sourced records or a 24-character ObjectId for uploaded records. Get it from a chat citation (`citations[*].recordId`) or from a `pipeshub_search` hit. Required when `mode` is `content` or `thread`.

startBlock.description: Read in order from this block — the value in a previous read's `Next:` line, or 0 to read from the top. In thread mode it applies to the record at `startRecord`.

startRecord.description: Thread mode: carry on a long thread from this record, with the `startBlock` given beside it in a previous read's `Next:` line.

tools.name: pipeshub_get_record_content

tools.description:
Vector / semantic search across the org's indexed documents.

**The default first step for a question about the org's knowledge**, and
for locating a document by name, topic, or phrase. Then read the records
that matter with `pipeshub_get_record_content` and answer from them;
search again with other wording or sources if the first results miss.
`pipeshub_chat`, where offered, is optional: it runs PipesHub's assistant
and returns an answer with citations to check.

For a full-document task (summarize, extract, review, "what does the doc
say?"), read the top hit with `mode:"content"`. Also: resolve a filename
into a `recordId` for `pipeshub_download_record`, or show the user a
ranked list of matching files when they ask "find / search for X".

Not for structural questions — what is under this epic, which pages are
in this space, what links to this ticket. Ranking by content cannot show
how records relate; use `pipeshub_get_record_content` `mode:"navigate"`.

**A ranked sample, never a complete list.** It returns the best-matching
records and a few passages of each — not every record that matches, not
every passage. Never count them to answer "how many" / "all" / "every";
navigate the record group instead, which reports its real total.

By default it searches everything. To search only some sources, pass
connector ids in `apps` and collection ids in `kb`.

Returns `records`, one per record, best first: `recordId`, name, type,
`webUrl`, source dates, `parent`, a ticket's or PR's `status` with
its date, linked records with theirs (`links`), `passagesFound` and up
to 3 `passages`. Results stay under 20,000 characters; if records were cut,
call again with `offset` set to `nextOffset`.

apps.description: Connector ids to search (for example a Jira or Google Drive connection). Get them from `pipeshub_sources`, where `kind` is "connector". Collection ids go in `kb`, not here.

createdAfter.description: Only records created in their source on or after this date. `YYYY-MM-DD` (that whole day, UTC) or an ISO 8601 datetime with a timezone, such as `2026-09-01T09:00:00Z`.

createdBefore.description: Only records created in their source on or before this date. A `YYYY-MM-DD` value includes that whole day.

kb.description: Collection (knowledge base) ids to search. Get them from `pipeshub_sources`, where `kind` is "knowledgeBase".

limit.description: Vector matches to fetch. Default 10. The tool asks for the query to be searched as written. A PipesHub server that ignores that option rewrites it instead and searches the rewrite plus a few variants, `limit` matches each, so one call can return more records than `limit`. 5–10 is enough to find a `recordId`.

modifiedAfter.description: Only records last changed in their source on or after this date. Use it for "what changed since …" and to leave out superseded documents.

modifiedBefore.description: Only records last changed in their source on or before this date.

offset.description: Records to skip. To read the next page of the same results, pass the previous call's `nextOffset` with the same other arguments.

query.description: Natural language query. Vector search across the org's indexed records.

tools.name: pipeshub_search

annotations.title: List PipesHub sources and AI models

tools.description:
Discover available chat sources and AI models in one call.

Returns up to three sections:

- `sources` — connectors (`kind: "connector"`) and collections
  (`kind: "knowledgeBase"`). For `pipeshub_search` and
  `pipeshub_chat`, put a connector `id` in `apps` and a collection
  `id` in `kb`. `sourcesTruncated: true` means the list stopped at
  1,000 sources. Readable ones carry `coverage`.
- `llmModels` — chat / generation models. Each item's `modelKey`
  is the value to pass on `pipeshub_chat` as `modelKey`. Pick
  `isDefault: true` unless the user asks for a specific model.
- `embeddingModels` — vector embedding models (only fetched when
  explicitly requested via `include`).

The model lists need the `config:read` scope. A token without it still
gets `sources`; the model sections are left out and `notes` says why.
Omit `modelKey` on `pipeshub_chat` to use the org's default model.

Call this once at the start of a session and cache the result —
sources and models change infrequently.

include.description: Which sections to fetch. Default: `["sources", "llmModels"]`. Add `embeddingModels` if the user is configuring re-embedding.

tools.name: pipeshub_sources
